title: A Performance-Portable Kilometer-Scale Global Ocean Model on ORISE and New Sunway Heterogeneous Supercomputers
problem: Global kilometer-scale ocean simulations demand immense computational power and must overcome the 1-simulated-year-per-day (SYPD) performance barrier while maintaining portability across diverse hardware architectures with different instruction sets and memory hierarchies.
motivation: Ocean general circulation models are essential for understanding multi-scale oceanic processes and climate change, but achieving kilometer-scale resolution requires exceptional computational resources.
method: LICOMK++ implements an ocean general circulation model using Kokkos, a performance portability framework that provides a single source codebase with hardware-specific backends. The authors enhanced Kokkos with Sunway architecture support, enabling execution on Sunway processors, CUDA/HIP GPUs, and ARM CPUs through abstracted parallel kernels and memory management.
key_novelty: First performance-portable global ocean general circulation model achieving kilometer-scale simulations across heterogeneous architectures (Sunway, GPUs, ARM CPUs) via a unified Kokkos codebase.
contributions: Extended Kokkos framework with native Sunway architecture support for scientific computing
Achieved 1.05-1.70 SYPD performance on supercomputers, surpassing the 1-SYPD threshold for global 1-km-resolution OGCMs
Demonstrated 54.8-55.6% parallel efficiency at scale across diverse heterogeneous supercomputing systems
First scientifically validated global 1-km-resolution ocean simulation reproducing realistic mesoscale and submesoscale structures

metrics.speedup: 1.05-1.70 SYPD on Sunway and ORISE supercomputers
metrics.accuracy: Successfully reproduces mesoscale and submesoscale ocean circulation structures

limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
